trial_name.text: Study CBAF312A2304 (A2304), the single pivotal Phase 3 trial

citations.quote: The applicant submitted data from one pivotal efficacy Phase 3 clinical trial, Study CBAF312A2304 (A2304 hereafter). This single study is supported by findings from a smaller, dose finding Phase 2 trial, CBAF312A2201 (A2201 hereafter).

nct.text: Not stated in the reviewed documents

citations.quote: The applicant submitted data from one pivotal efficacy Phase 3 clinical trial, Study CBAF312A2304 (A2304 hereafter). This single study is supported by findings from a smaller, dose finding Phase 2 trial, CBAF312A2201 (A2201 hereafter).
This was a double-blind, placebo-controlled, Phase 3 safety and efficacy study (Study A2304) in patients with SPMS.

design.text: Multi-national, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven study; patients randomized 2:1 to siponimod (titrated to 2 mg oral daily) or placebo

citations.quote: Study A2304 was a multi-national, multi-center, randomized, double blind, placebo-controlled study, intended to evaluate the safety and efficacy of siponimod in patients with protocol-defined SPMS. Study A2304 utilized a 6-day titration schedule to achieve an oral maintenance dose of 2 mg daily. The treatment duration in Study A2304 was variable (up to 37 months) because the trial was event-driven
There were 1651 patients randomized in a 2:1 ratio as follows: 1105 patients were randomized to siponimod, and 546 patients were randomized to placebo.

population.text: Patients with protocol-defined secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (SPMS), with baseline EDSS of 3.0 to 6.5

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint was time to 3-month confirmed disability progression (CDP) as measured by the EDSS

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint of Study A2304 was the time to 3-month confirmed disability progression, as measured by the EDSS.
There were 1651 patients randomized in a 2:1 ratio as follows: 1105 patients were randomized to siponimod, and 546 patients were randomized to placebo.

result.text: 3-month CDP occurred in 288/1096 (26.3%) siponimod vs 173/545 (31.7%) placebo; 21.2% relative risk reduction, 5.4% absolute risk reduction, hazard ratio 0.79 (95% CI 0.65, 0.95), p=0.0134

indication.text: Treatment of relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS), to include clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease, in adults

citations.quote: MAYZENT is indicated for the treatment of relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS), to include clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease, in adults.

target_moa.text: Siponimod is a sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) receptor modulator that binds selectively to the S1P1 and S1P5 receptors; it promotes internalization and degradation of S1P1 receptors, acting as a functional antagonist that reduces recirculation of T-cells into the CNS to limit central inflammation

citations.quote: Siponimod is a sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) receptor modulator that binds selectively to the S1P1 and S1P5 receptors, proposed by the applicant for the treatment of secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (MS).

Mechanism of action	Siponimod promotes internalization and degradation of S1P1 receptors, thereby acting as a functional antagonist on S1P1. This antagonism is proposed to reduce the recirculation of T-cells into the central nervous system (CNS) to limit central inflammation.

This application contains data in support of the safety and effectiveness of siponimod, a sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) receptor modulator selective for the S1P1 and S1P5 receptor subtypes, administered daily as an oral tablet, proposed by the applicant for the treatment of secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (SPMS). key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >10%) are headache (15% vs 14% placebo), hypertension (13% vs 9%), and transaminase increases (11% vs 3%); other reactions include falls (11% vs 10%), peripheral edema (8% vs 4%), and bradycardia (6% vs 3%). Serious risks include bradyarrhythmia and atrioventricular conduction delays, infections, macular edema, and a decline in pulmonary function (FEV1).

detail.text: CYP2C9 genotype testing is required prior to treatment to guide dosing and identify contraindicated CYP2C9*3/*3 patients, but no FDA-cleared or -approved test for CYP2C9 variants to direct siponimod use is currently available

citations.quote: Test patients for CYP2C9 variants to determine CYP2C9 genotype [see *Dosage and Administration* (2.2, 2.3), *Contraindications* (4), and *Use in Specific Populations* (8.6)]. An FDA-cleared or -approved test for the detection of CYP2C9 variants to direct the use of siponimod is not currently available.

After a rolling review was granted in January 2018, the submission of New Drug Application #209884 was complete on June 28, 2018.

requirement.text: 3591-3: A prospective, parallel cohort study in patients with relapsing forms of MS to assess the potentially serious risk of pulmonary toxicity, comparing patients newly prescribed siponimod with patients receiving another MS drug

citations.quote: 3591-3 A prospective, parallel cohort study in patients with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis to assess the potentially serious risk of pulmonary toxicity. The two cohorts should consist of patients newly prescribed siponimod and patients receiving another drug used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis.

requirement.text: 3591-4: A prospective pregnancy exposure registry cohort analyses comparing maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women with MS exposed to siponimod during pregnancy with two unexposed control populations

citations.quote: 3591-4 Conduct prospective pregnancy exposure registry cohort analyses in the United States that compare the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women with multiple sclerosis exposed to siponimod during pregnancy with two unexposed control populations: one consisting of women with multiple sclerosis who have not been exposed to siponimod before or during pregnancy, and the other consisting of women without multiple sclerosis.

requirement.text: 3591-5: A pregnancy outcomes study using a different design (e.g., retrospective cohort or case control) to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, and small-for-gestational-age births in women exposed to siponimod during pregnancy versus an unexposed control population

citations.quote: 3591-5 Conduct a pregnancy outcomes study using a different study design than provided for in PMR 3591-4 (for example, a retrospective cohort study using claims or electronic medical record data or a case control study) to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, and small-for-gestational-age births in women exposed to siponimod during pregnancy compared to an unexposed control population.

requirement.text: 3591-6: Establish an in-vitro diagnostic device to guide the use of siponimod, detecting at a minimum the *2 and *3 alleles in CYP2C9 and identifying patients homozygous for the CYP2C9*3/*3 genotype

citations.quote: 3591-6 Establish an in-vitro diagnostic device to guide the use of siponimod in patients with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis. The device should detect, at a minimum, the presence of the *2 and *3 alleles in cytochrome P450 2C9 (CYP2C9). The device should detect patients homozygous for the CYP2C9 *3/*3 genotype with statistical confidence.

basis.text: A Fast Track application for the indication of the treatment of SPMS was granted in September 2012

citations.quote: In April 2012, the applicant submitted the protocol for Study A2304 with a request for a SPA. SPA agreement was reached in August 2012. A Fast Track application for the indication of the treatment of SPMS was granted in September 2012,

summary.text: Siponimod (a new molecular entity) received Fast Track designation for the SPMS indication in September 2012 and was approved on the first review cycle based on the single pivotal Phase 3 trial A2304; the application was not referred to an advisory committee. This was a standard (non-accelerated) approval with no breakthrough, orphan, or priority review designations noted.

description.text: Labeling update to add lesser identified CYP2C9 polymorphisms and amend vaccine recommendations; no new indication or population added

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for an update to the prescribing information (PI) to include lesser identified CYP2C9 polymorphisms in Use in Specific Populations (8.6) and Clinical Pharmacology (12.5) sections, and to amend the current vaccine recommendations to prescribers in the Warnings and Precautions (5.1) and Drug Interactions (7.4) sections of the PI.
